# OpenRigGraph

> Renderer-neutral character rig graph runtime documentation. Running examples
> requires an existing ORG SDK; this is a docs-only distribution.

- [Getting started](https://zukunfcs.github.io/OpenRigGraph-docs/getting_started.html)
- [Agent workflow](https://zukunfcs.github.io/OpenRigGraph-docs/porting/agent_workflow.html)
- [Synthetic tutorial](https://zukunfcs.github.io/OpenRigGraph-docs/porting/tutorial.html)
- [Graph nodes](https://zukunfcs.github.io/OpenRigGraph-docs/nodes/index.html)
- [Maya integration](https://zukunfcs.github.io/OpenRigGraph-docs/maya/index.html)

# docs/source/agents/using_skills.rst

Use the discovery and porting skills
====================================

The documentation distribution includes reusable, source-neutral skill files:

* :download:`Discovery skill <../../agent_skills/org_rig_discovery/SKILL.md>`.
* :download:`Porting skill <../../agent_skills/org_rig_porting/SKILL.md>`.

Supply the documentation/SDK root, requested scene, matching mayapy/plug-in,
output directory, intended domain, and acceptance tolerances. Example assignment:

.. code-block:: text

   Read the ORG node reference and porting skill in the documentation bundle.
   Use my existing SDK and matching Maya environment to port the supplied scene.
   Preserve animator controls and editable curves. Record input/output ownership,
   units, spaces, unsupported dependencies, and a replayable verification packet.
   Do not treat successful export as proof of deformation/animation parity.

Review graph validation, output coverage, independent source comparisons,
approximation domains/errors, temporal behavior, authoring, and relocation.
Keep source-specific identifiers and probes in private working artifacts.


# docs/source/design_notes.rst

Runtime design
==============

Graph IR is the portable interchange/debugging representation. Compilation
resolves endpoints, orders required dependencies, lowers operations, and produces
an evaluation module. Instances own mutable controls and output state. Compile
once for repeated evaluation and inspect lowered instructions when tracing errors.

The runtime owns explicit contracts; exporters own DCC discovery, extraction,
unit/space adaptation, and validation against the source. Maya integration nodes
bridge numeric/packed/geometry boundaries without implying full-DG compatibility.
External operators supply their behavior through registered providers/resources.

Exact primitives, scoped behaviors, and sampled/fitted representations coexist.
Their error evidence and dependency boundaries remain explicit. See
:doc:`porting/design_decisions` for invented representation decisions and
:doc:`reference/embedding` for library ownership.


# docs/source/getting_started.rst

Getting started
===============

Runtime access
--------------

This is a documentation-only distribution. Running examples requires an existing
OpenRigGraph SDK or authorized source checkout. This repository does not contain
the runtime library, executable, or Maya plug-in. Do not build ORG from the
documentation repository.

Locate ``orgctl`` (``orgctl.exe`` on Windows), the public header/library for
embedding, and a plug-in built for your Maya version. Put ``orgctl`` on PATH or
substitute its full path. Maya and source plug-ins are separate dependencies.

.. code-block:: console

   git clone https://github.com/ZukunFCS/OpenRigGraph-docs.git
   cd OpenRigGraph-docs
   orgctl validate examples/graph/addDoubleLinear.json
   orgctl eval examples/graph/addDoubleLinear.json --output json

The result is ``{"result": 3}``. Continue with the
:doc:`synthetic character tutorial <porting/tutorial>`.

Build from authorized source
----------------------------

Run from the ORG source root, not the documentation root. Requirements are
CMake 3.25+, a C++20 toolchain, and the configured JSON dependency.
On Windows use an installed Visual Studio C++ toolchain:

.. code-block:: powershell

   cmake -S . -B build_verify -G "Visual Studio 18 2026"
   cmake --build build_verify --config Release --parallel 4
   ctest --test-dir build_verify -C Release --output-on-failure
   .\build_verify\Release\orgctl.exe eval examples\graph\addDoubleLinear.json --output json

Select the corresponding CMake generator if using another installed Visual
Studio version. The source rejects the mutable Scoop LLVM ``current`` toolchain
path; use MSVC or an explicitly versioned toolchain.

For the opt-in Maya integration, supply the actual Maya installation:

.. code-block:: powershell

   cmake -S . -B build_maya -G "Visual Studio 18 2026" -DORG_BUILD_MAYA_PLUGIN=ON -DORG_MAYA_ROOT="C:/Program Files/Autodesk/Maya2024"
   cmake --build build_maya --config Release --parallel 4

Use a separate build tree per Maya ABI. Successful compilation does not prove
compatibility with another version. See :doc:`release` and :doc:`maya/contracts`.

Build the documentation
-----------------------

The documentation build needs neither Maya nor the SDK:

.. code-block:: console

   python -m venv .venv
   python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
   python -m sphinx -n -W -b html docs/source docs/build/html

Activate the virtual environment before installing requirements: Windows uses
``.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`` and POSIX uses ``source .venv/bin/activate``.
Open ``docs/build/html/index.html``. API details are in :doc:`reference/cli`
and :doc:`reference/embedding`.


# docs/source/index.rst

OpenRigGraph documentation
==========================

OpenRigGraph (ORG) is a renderer-neutral graph interchange and compiled runtime
for portable character evaluation. Exporters translate supported source behavior
into explicit numeric, transform, curve, surface, and scoped geometry contracts.

Start with :doc:`getting_started`, or give an agent
:doc:`porting/agent_workflow` and a source scene plus the required SDK.
ORG is not an automatic evaluator for every Maya dependency graph node.

This reference covers **59 graph types, 7 aliases, and 14 Maya integration
types**, plus the C, Python, and command-line APIs. Runtime support, exporter
coverage, and verified source parity are distinct claims.

.. toctree::
   :maxdepth: 2
   :caption: Start here

   getting_started
   porting/index
   agents/index

.. toctree::
   :maxdepth: 2
   :caption: API reference

   nodes/index
   maya/index
   reference/index

.. toctree::
   :maxdepth: 1
   :caption: Design and release

   porting/design_decisions
   design_notes
   release

Machine-readable documentation
------------------------------

Download the :download:`node and API catalog <_generated/node_catalog.json>`.
The documentation repository supplies ``llms.txt`` and ``llms-full.txt`` for
agents and independent examples under ``examples/``.


# docs/source/maya/contracts.rst

Maya integration contracts
==========================

Load a plug-in compiled for the actual Maya ABI before creating ORG nodes or
opening a scene containing them. The node pages list registered attributes from
the current source snapshot. All integration nodes are separate from portable
Graph IR type names. Creation alone does not prepare required data or verify
deformation.

Packed layouts and typed boundaries
-----------------------------------

Graph controller and output orders define numeric array indices. XYZ points
use three values; matrices use sixteen row-major values. Distinguish packed
graph outputs, deformation points, influence matrices, and mesh objects. Never
connect buffers based only on their shared double-array storage type.

Input bundles preserve graph defaults and logical indices. Matrix inputs declare
their controller base indices. Matrix scatter input modes distinguish matrix
blocks from other supported transform layouts; preserve the mode and expected
value count generated by the SDK wiring helper.

Scalar scatter selects number, angle, distance, boolean, and integer output
groups using corresponding index arrays. Packed angles are degrees and packed
distances are centimeters; the node produces Maya typed plugs. Boolean values
must be 0 or 1 and integer lanes must contain integral int32 values. Invalid
counts/indices/typed values fail compute. Do not add a second unit conversion
after a correctly typed boundary.

Paths and reloads
-----------------

Absolute paths identify explicit resources. A plain relative path resolves
beside the current scene; give the scene its intended filename before the first
demand. ``@package/relative/path`` resolves under ``OPENRIGGRAPH_PACKAGE_ROOT``
when that root is configured. Load the plug-in and establish package roots before
opening delivered scenes. After replacing data at the same path, increment the
node's reloadToken where provided. Package-relative resources must remain inside
the delivered package.

Geometry packages
-----------------

Package loaders validate versions, point counts/ranges, topology, finite values,
and operation-specific fields. SDK producers capture source geometry and write
these layouts; the node does not discover a character automatically.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1

   * - Node
     - Public package contract
     - Main ownership boundary
   * - openRigGraphBlendShapeBatch
     - openriggraph.blendshape_batch.v1
     - Sparse target groups, weight indices, in-betweens, and packed XYZ points.
   * - openRigGraphSoftModBatch
     - openriggraph.softmod_batch.v1
     - Ordered captured regions/weights and geometry/transform spaces.
   * - openRigGraphSkinBatch
     - openriggraph.skin_batch.v1
     - Influence/bind/weight layout, input mesh geometry, optional packed pre-skin points.
   * - openRigGraphUvPinBatch
     - openriggraph.uvpin_batch.v1
     - Captured mesh/UV attachments and packed point/frame layout.
   * - openRigGraphPointMapBatch
     - openriggraph.point_map_batch.v1 / v2
     - Declared mapping, driver/input meshes, matrix/radius data.
   * - openRigGraphFaceGeometryBatch
     - SDK-produced program; direct public package authoring is not specified
     - Ordered geometry program and its declared input/output buffers.

Use matching-version SDK producers, then verify the public node interface and
delivered geometry. Do not guess serialized fields from example scenes. The
public Python blendshape/face APIs expose reusable data contracts where available.

Cache authoring and playback
----------------------------

Keep editable controls/curves. A curve cache is a prepared numeric data stream
with a declared time range, row layout, interpolation policy, and reload token.
Curve-cache interpolation is 0 exact, 1 nearest (default), or 2 linear.
A double-array switch chooses live or cached values; it does not validate cache
freshness. Invalidate after relevant edits, rebuild before cached mode, and test
fractional/out-of-range times using the chosen policy. See the Python cache and
face-mode APIs and the hypothetical playback decision guide.

Validate interfaces with
:download:`check_interfaces.py <../../../examples/maya/check_interfaces.py>`
and verify deformation using :doc:`../porting/tutorial`. Missing resources may
emit compute errors even when DG nodes can be created; those are dependencies,
not successful evaluation.

# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphBlendShapeBatch.rst

openRigGraphBlendShapeBatch
===========================

Evaluate sparse blendshape target groups into packed points.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphBlendShapeBatch``.

When to use
-----------

Use when captured sparse targets and in-betweens share a stable point layout.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - packagePath
     - string
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Path to the node's explicitly prepared geometry package. Short name: ``pp``.
   * - reloadToken
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Increment after replacing a resource at the same path to force reload. Short name: ``rt``.
   * - packedValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Packed scalar data with indices defined by the graph/package contract. Short name: ``pv``.
   * - outputPoints
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Packed XYZ points in package order; every point occupies three doubles. Short name: ``op``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Package bases, target weight indices, sparse vertex indices, and XYZ deltas must agree. Packed output is points, not a mesh object.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: python

   import maya.cmds as cmds
   node = cmds.createNode("openRigGraphBlendShapeBatch", name="exampleBlendShapeBatch")

This creates the DG interface; it does not prepare a graph, cache, or geometry package. Configure the listed inputs before requesting its outputs.

Download the :download:`synthetic Maya interface checks <../../../examples/maya/check_interfaces.py>` and the :doc:`complete porting tutorial <../porting/tutorial>`.

Validation
----------

Check actual attribute types and logical indices, then compare the connected output across changing inputs and fractional times. Node creation alone is not deformation parity. Reject stale/missing resources and layouts that do not match the package.


# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphCurveCache.rst

openRigGraphCurveCache
======================

Read sparse cached numeric rows using a time input.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphCurveCache``.

When to use
-----------

Use for verified cached playback with a known output layout.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - cachePath
     - string
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Path to the prepared numeric cache. Short name: ``cp``.
   * - reloadToken
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Increment after replacing a resource at the same path to force reload. Short name: ``rt``.
   * - time
     - time
     - 0.0
     - input / configuration; Evaluation time in the cache's declared time convention. Short name: ``tm``.
   * - interpolation
     - integer enum
     - 1
     - input / configuration; 0 exact sample, 1 nearest (default), 2 linear; see integration contracts. Short name: ``ip``.
   * - outputValues
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Computed output values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ov``.
   * - sampleIndex
     - integer
     - computed
     - output; Declared sample index; indices address the packed input/package layout. Short name: ``si``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Cache time range, fractional-time policy, path reload, and stale-cache detection must be explicit. Preserve editable source curves for authoring.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: python

   import maya.cmds as cmds
   node = cmds.createNode("openRigGraphCurveCache", name="exampleCurveCache")

This creates the DG interface; it does not prepare a graph, cache, or geometry package. Configure the listed inputs before requesting its outputs.

Download the :download:`synthetic Maya interface checks <../../../examples/maya/check_interfaces.py>` and the :doc:`complete porting tutorial <../porting/tutorial>`.

Validation
----------

Check actual attribute types and logical indices, then compare the connected output across changing inputs and fractional times. Node creation alone is not deformation parity. Reject stale/missing resources and layouts that do not match the package.


# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphDoubleArraySwitch.rst

openRigGraphDoubleArraySwitch
=============================

Select between live and cached typed double-array streams.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphDoubleArraySwitch``.

When to use
-----------

Use at a deliberate live-authoring/cached-playback boundary.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - cachedValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node cached values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``cv``.
   * - liveValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node live values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``lv``.
   * - liveMode
     - boolean
     - false
     - input / configuration; Node live mode; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``lm``.
   * - outputValues
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Computed output values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ov``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Selection does not make a stale cache valid. Invalidate caches after relevant input or curve edits and rebuild before switching back.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: python

   import maya.cmds as cmds
   node = cmds.createNode("openRigGraphDoubleArraySwitch", name="exampleDoubleArraySwitch")

This creates the DG interface; it does not prepare a graph, cache, or geometry package. Configure the listed inputs before requesting its outputs.

Download the :download:`synthetic Maya interface checks <../../../examples/maya/check_interfaces.py>` and the :doc:`complete porting tutorial <../porting/tutorial>`.

Validation
----------

Check actual attribute types and logical indices, then compare the connected output across changing inputs and fractional times. Node creation alone is not deformation parity. Reject stale/missing resources and layouts that do not match the package.


# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphEvaluator.rst

openRigGraphEvaluator
=====================

Evaluate a graph with Maya numeric inputs and indexed numeric outputs.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphEvaluator``.

When to use
-----------

Use for a straightforward graph-to-Maya DG connection.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - graphPath
     - string
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Graph JSON or supported compiled-module path; use a relocatable package path. Short name: ``gp``.
   * - reloadToken
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Increment after replacing a resource at the same path to force reload. Short name: ``rt``.
   * - inputValue
     - double logical array
     - 0.0
     - input / configuration; Controller value at its graph logical index. Short name: ``iv``.
   * - inputMatrix
     - matrix4x4 (double) logical array
     - identity
     - input / configuration; Matrix input; preserve declared input-space convention. Short name: ``im``.
   * - packedInput
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node packed input; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``pi``.
   * - outputValue
     - double logical array
     - computed
     - output; Computed output value; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ov``.
   * - packedOutput
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Graph outputs in the declared graph-output order. Short name: ``po``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Keep controller/output ordering identical to graph metadata. graphPath and reloadToken govern resource reloads.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: python

   import maya.cmds as cmds
   node = cmds.createNode("openRigGraphEvaluator", name="exampleEvaluator")

This creates the DG interface; it does not prepare a graph, cache, or geometry package. Configure the listed inputs before requesting its outputs.

Download the :download:`synthetic Maya interface checks <../../../examples/maya/check_interfaces.py>` and the :doc:`complete porting tutorial <../porting/tutorial>`.

Validation
----------

Check actual attribute types and logical indices, then compare the connected output across changing inputs and fractional times. Node creation alone is not deformation parity. Reject stale/missing resources and layouts that do not match the package.


# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphFaceGeometryBatch.rst

openRigGraphFaceGeometryBatch
=============================

Execute an explicitly packaged sequence of supported geometry operations.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphFaceGeometryBatch``.

When to use
-----------

Use when multiple point/deformation operations can share a declared schedule and buffer layout.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - programPath
     - string
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node program path; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``pp``.
   * - reloadToken
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Increment after replacing a resource at the same path to force reload. Short name: ``rt``.
   * - packedValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Packed scalar data with indices defined by the graph/package contract. Short name: ``pv``.
   * - inputGeometry
     - mesh logical array
     - MObject::kNullObj
     - input / configuration; Node input geometry; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ig``.
   * - outputGeometry
     - mesh logical array
     - computed
     - output; Computed output geometry; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``og``.
   * - auxiliaryGeometry
     - mesh logical array
     - computed
     - output; Computed auxiliary geometry; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ag``.
   * - outputPoints
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Packed XYZ points in package order; every point occupies three doubles. Short name: ``op``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Validate operation ordering, buffer ranges, and external inputs. The node name does not imply an automatic character exporter.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: python

This creates the DG interface; it does not prepare a graph, cache, or geometry package. Configure the listed inputs before requesting its outputs.

Download the :download:`synthetic Maya interface checks <../../../examples/maya/check_interfaces.py>` and the :doc:`complete porting tutorial <../porting/tutorial>`.

Validation
----------

Check actual attribute types and logical indices, then compare the connected output across changing inputs and fractional times. Node creation alone is not deformation parity. Reject stale/missing resources and layouts that do not match the package.


# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphInputBundle.rst

openRigGraphInputBundle
=======================

Pack Maya scalar input plugs into a typed double array.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphInputBundle``.

When to use
-----------

Use when a packed evaluator or geometry operation consumes a shared control array.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - defaultValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node default values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``dv``.
   * - inputValue
     - double logical array
     - 0.0
     - input / configuration; Controller value at its graph logical index. Short name: ``iv``.
   * - inputMatrix
     - matrix4x4 (double) logical array
     - identity
     - input / configuration; Matrix input; preserve declared input-space convention. Short name: ``im``.
   * - matrixBaseIndex
     - integer logical array
     - -1
     - input / configuration; Controller-array base index assigned to each matrix input. Short name: ``mbi``.
   * - outputValues
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Computed output values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ov``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Logical array indices are part of the graph layout; do not compact them.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: python

   import maya.cmds as cmds

This creates the DG interface; it does not prepare a graph, cache, or geometry package. Configure the listed inputs before requesting its outputs.

# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphMatrixScatter.rst

openRigGraphMatrixScatter
=========================

Expose selected matrices from packed evaluation output.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphMatrixScatter``.

When to use
-----------

Use to connect matrix blocks into Maya transform/deformer inputs.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - inputValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node input values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``iv``.
   * - jointCount
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Declared joint count; must match the corresponding packed layout. Short name: ``jc``.
   * - expectedInputValueCount
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Declared expected input value count; must match the corresponding packed layout. Short name: ``eivc``.
   * - inputMode
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Node input mode; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``im``.
   * - rotateOrder
     - integer logical array
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Node rotate order; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ro``.
   * - jointOrientValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node joint orient values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``jov``.
   * - outputMatrix
     - matrix4x4 (double) logical array
     - computed
     - output; Computed output matrix; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``om``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Each matrix block contains 16 row-major values. Check base indices and graph output units.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage
-----

.. code-block:: python

   import maya.cmds as cmds
   node = cmds.createNode("openRigGraphMatrixScatter", name="exampleMatrixScatter")

This creates the DG interface; it does not prepare a graph, cache, or geometry package. Configure the listed inputs before requesting its outputs.

Download the :download:`synthetic Maya interface checks <../../../examples/maya/check_interfaces.py>` and the :doc:`complete porting tutorial <../porting/tutorial>`.

# docs/source/maya/openRigGraphMeshVertexBundle.rst

openRigGraphMeshVertexBundle
============================

Extract indexed mesh point data as a packed numeric array.

**Layer:** Maya integration node. **Type identifier:** ``openRigGraphMeshVertexBundle``.

When to use
-----------

Use to feed reusable geometry evaluation with a declared support vertex set.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - inputValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Node input values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``iv``.
   * - inputMesh
     - mesh
     - MObject::kNullObj
     - input / configuration; Node input mesh; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``im``.
   * - worldMatrix
     - matrix4x4 (double)
     - identity
     - input / configuration; Node world matrix; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``wm``.
   * - baseIndex
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Declared base index; indices address the packed input/package layout. Short name: ``bi``.
   * - vertexIndices
     - integer[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Declared vertex indices; indices address the packed input/package layout. Short name: ``vi``.
   * - outputValues
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Computed output values; see the wiring and package contract below. Short name: ``ov``.

Wiring and resource contract
----------------------------

Keep topology and vertex identifiers stable. Coordinate space follows the declared mesh/matrix input boundary.

See :doc:`shared integration contracts <contracts>` for packed indices, typed units, reloads, package schemas, and safe reconnection.

Usage

openRigGraphRuntime
===================

Evaluate a compiled graph through compact scalar, matrix, and curve input interfaces.

When to use
-----------

Use for packed runtime wiring with output-generation and changed-influence tracking.

Attributes
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - graphPath
     - string
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Graph JSON or supported compiled-module path; use a relocatable package path. Short name: ``gp``.
   * - reloadToken
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Increment after replacing a resource at the same path to force reload. Short name: ``rt``.
   * - inputValue
     - double logical array
     - 0.0
     - input / configuration; Controller value at its graph logical index. Short name: ``iv``.
   * - inputMatrix
     - matrix4x4 (double) logical array
     - identity
     - input / configuration; Matrix input; preserve declared input-space convention. Short name: ``im``.
   * - matrixBaseIndex
     - integer logical array
     - -1
     - input / configuration; Controller-array base index assigned to each matrix input. Short name: ``mbi``.

     - empty
     - input / configuration; Graph controller indices for the corresponding curveValues entries. Short name: ``ci``.
   * - curveValues
     - double[]
     - empty
     - input / configuration; Curve values ordered exactly like curveIndices. Short name: ``cv``.
   * - expectedOutputValueCount
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Expected packed scalar count; validate against the loaded module. Short name: ``eovc``.
   * - matrixOutputCount
     - integer
     - 0
     - input / configuration; Number of matrix output blocks used by change tracking. Short name: ``moc``.
   * - changeEpsilon
     - double
     - 0.0
     - input / configuration; Nonnegative change-detection threshold; does not change graph math. Short name: ``ce``.
   * - resolvedControls
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Resolved graph control array, including defaults and bound inputs. Short name: ``rc``.
   * - packedOutput
     - double[]
     - computed
     - output; Graph outputs in the declared graph-output order. Short name: ``po``.
   * - outputGeneration
     - integer
     - computed
     - output; Generation marker used to coordinate output consumers. Short name: ``og``.
   * - changedInfluenceIndices
     - integer[]
     - computed
     - output; Indices whose output matrix blocks changed beyond changeEpsilon. Short name: ``cii``.

# docs/source/nodes/aimConstraint.rst

aimConstraint
=============

Aim a constrained orientation toward an ordered, weighted target set.

**Aliases:** none.

   * - target[i].targetTranslateX/Y/Z; target[i].targetParentMatrix; target[i].targetWeight
     - number / matrix endpoints
     - target defaults
     - World target reconstruction and weights.

# docs/source/nodes/animation_contracts.rst

Animation curve contracts
=========================

Simple keys
-----------

Supply ordered keys with input/value (aliases time/x and output/y), or matching
x/values arrays. Interpolation is linear, step/constant, or smooth/smoothstep.
This simplified response curve does not reconstruct all Maya tangent modes.

Native tangents
---------------

nativeCurve.keys is a nonempty ordered array with finite input/value and native
incoming/outgoing tangent vectors ``in_xy`` and ``out_xy`` (two numbers each).
``out_type`` defaults to 2; preserve the source-exported tangent type code.
``nativeCurve.weighted`` defaults false and selects weighted tangent evaluation.
Inputs are strictly increasing; a single numeric value key is a constant.
Preserve exporter version and numeric units;
the native representation is evaluated separately from simple interpolation.
Use the SDK curve exporter and maya_curve.evaluate_native_curve for a matching
reference representation. See :doc:`../reference/python/maya_curve`.

Infinity and verification
-------------------------

preInfinity/postInfinity accept 0 (constant) or 3 (cycle); other modes fail
compilation. Test both ends, endpoints, fractional coordinates, tangent
transitions, and repeated cycles. Frame-only playback does not establish
fractional-time equivalence.

   * - weights
     - number[2]
     - [1,1]
     - Static weight defaults.
   * - interpolateMode
     - integer
     - 0
     - Captured blend interpolation mode; verify non-default modes against the source.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - output
     - number
     - computed
     - Scalar result.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/animBlendNodeAdditive.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/animBlendNodeAdditive.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/animBlendNodeAdditive.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **2**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Preserve the declared input/output types, source units, and domain. Semantic validation is performed by the runtime compiler, not only the structural JSON schema.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

# docs/source/nodes/ApproxNode.rst

.. _node-ApproxNode:

ApproxNode
==========

Evaluate a deterministic sparse-linear output model.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Validated model contract.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use for a compact affine response only after separate verification over the declared input domain.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - declared input names
     - number endpoints
     - required by terms
     - Named model features.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - backend
     - string
     - sparse_linear
     - Only sparse_linear is supported.
   * - outputs
     - named output-record object
     - required
     - Each output contains bias and weights or terms; terms contain input/weight.
   * - provenance
     - object
     - exporter requirement
     - Record domain, fit/validation split, sample counts, and error metrics in private port artifacts.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - declared output names
     - number
     - computed
     - bias + sum(weight * input).

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/ApproxNode.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/ApproxNode.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/ApproxNode.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **7**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

ApproxNode shares the sparse-linear compiler path. Neither name proves approximation quality; report residuals on held-out observations.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.


# docs/source/nodes/axisAngleToQuat.rst

.. _node-axisAngleToQuat:

axisAngleToQuat
===============

Convert an axis and angle into an XYZW quaternion.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Exact numeric primitive.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use at an orientation representation boundary; keep XYZW component order and multiplication direction explicit.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - inputAxisX/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - [1,0,0]
     - Rotation axis.
   * - inputAngle
     - number endpoint
     - 0
     - Angle in the selected angle unit.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - anglesInDegrees
     - boolean
     - true
     - Set false for radian-valued Euler/angle channels.
   * - rotateOrder
     - string
     - xyz
     - xyz, yzx, zxy, xzy, yxz, or zyx; check node-specific integer order fields.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - outputQuatX/Y/Z/W
     - number
     - computed
     - Euler or quaternion components.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/axisAngleToQuat.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/axisAngleToQuat.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/axisAngleToQuat.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **1**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Quaternion sign and Euler wrap can differ while describing the same orientation. Compare transformed bases or angular distance, not only raw component subtraction.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

composeMatrix
=============

Compose a row-vector affine matrix from transform channels.

**Aliases:** ``MatrixComposeNode``.

When to use
-----------

Use for live transform expressions, including supported joint-orientation and scale-compensation terms.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - inputTranslateX/Y/Z; inputRotateX/Y/Z; inputScaleX/Y/Z; inputShearX/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - 0; scale=1
     - Transform components; matching vector parameters supply defaults.
   * - jointOrientX/Y/Z; rotateAxisX/Y/Z; inverseScaleX/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - 0; inverseScale=1
     - Joint and rotation-basis terms.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - anglesInDegrees
     - boolean
     - true
     - Set false for radian-valued Euler/angle channels.
   * - rotateOrder
     - string
     - xyz
     - xyz, yzx, zxy, xzy, yxz, or zyx; check node-specific integer order fields.
   * - segmentScaleCompensate
     - boolean
     - false
     - Enable supported inverse-scale compensation.
   * - inputRotateDoublePrecision; jointOrientDoublePrecision
     - booleans
     - false
     - Preserve double-precision parameter paths where implemented.
   * - scaleEpsilon
     - number
     - 0
     - Scale handling epsilon.

   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning

     - number; i=0..15
     - computed
     - Row-major matrix element; a whole outputMatrix endpoint is accepted by matrix consumers.

----------------------

   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/composeMatrix.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **2**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Matrices use row vectors and translation elements 12..14. Joint orientation, rotate axis, shear, and inherited scale are separate terms; do not replace them with a neutral snapshot.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

Related: :ref:`decomposeMatrix <node-decomposeMatrix>`, :ref:`multMatrix <node-multMatrix>`.

# docs/source/nodes/contracts.rst

Shared graph-node contracts
===========================

Endpoints and values
--------------------

Inputs resolve numbers, controller names, node.outputPin strings, or explicit
endpoint objects. Matrix/vector values use declared channels; supported matrix
consumers can accept a whole-matrix endpoint. Do not assume all Maya compound
plugs are universally supported. Logical array indices remain significant.

Use inputs for live endpoints and params for static configuration. The parser
also merges unreserved top-level node fields into params. Canonical aliases are
listed in :doc:`index`. Compilation is demand-driven from declared outputs;
exercise every required output rather than relying on unused nodes' presence.

Units and precision
-------------------

Matrices are row-major, use row vectors, and store translation in elements
12..14. A matrix is sixteen values. Vector/quaternion component order is XYZ/XYZW.
Transform/quaternion nodes use degrees when their anglesInDegrees contract
defaults true. angleBetween and scalar trigonometry return/use radians.
Maya typed angles use internal radians and distances use centimeters.
Curve numeric units must be exported explicitly.

Float and double C entry points coexist. A double interface does not guarantee
all kernels/parameter paths preserve arbitrary precision. Verify sensitive
transforms and delivered deformation. Test finite values, zero weights/scales,
division by zero, zero vectors, coincident aims, singular matrices, repeated
curve coordinates, and degenerate geometry if they belong to the required domain.

Support claims
--------------

Exact primitives evaluate defined formulas. Scoped nodes require documented
basis/topology/settings and source parity. RBF/model/sampled nodes evaluate
declared representations; their approximation quality is separate evidence.
External operators require provider/resource bindings. orgctl validate checks
semantic compilation, not DCC behavior or final character geometry.

# docs/source/nodes/decomposeMatrix.rst

.. _node-decomposeMatrix:

decomposeMatrix
===============

Extract translation, scale, shear, Euler rotation, and quaternion components from an affine matrix.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Scoped affine decomposition.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use at a matrix-to-channel boundary; choose the source rotate order and compare orientation across wrap boundaries.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - inputMatrix (alias matrix)
     - matrix endpoint
     - required for computed decomposition
     - Affine matrix to decompose.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - anglesInDegrees
     - boolean
     - true
     - Set false for radian-valued Euler/angle channels.
   * - rotateOrder
     - string
     - xyz
     - xyz, yzx, zxy, xzy, yxz, or zyx; check node-specific integer order fields.
   * - translate/translation/outputTranslate; scale/outputScale; shear/outputShear
     - number[3]
     - absent
     - Explicit exported component overrides take precedence.
   * - rotate/rotation/outputRotate; quaternion/quat/outputQuat
     - number[3] / number[4]
     - absent
     - Explicit orientation overrides.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - outputTranslateX/Y/Z; outputScaleX/Y/Z; outputShearX/Y/Z
     - number
     - computed
     - Affine components.
   * - outputRotateX/Y/Z; outputQuatX/Y/Z/W
     - number
     - computed
     - Euler and XYZW quaternion outputs.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/decomposeMatrix.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/decomposeMatrix.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/decomposeMatrix.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **0**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Rotation is evaluated from connected matrices in the current runtime; it is not restricted to baked rotation outputs.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

# docs/source/nodes/index.rst

Graph node reference
====================

Every entry below is a runtime-accepted type with a documented authoring contract. Source-node detection and exporter support are separate capabilities.

# docs/source/nodes/inverseMatrix.rst

.. _node-inverseMatrix:

inverseMatrix
=============

Invert a supported affine matrix.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Scoped affine inverse.

**Aliases:** ``MatrixInverseNode``.

When to use
-----------

Use for parent/world-space inversion; check singular scales before relying on the result.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - inputMatrix (alias matrix)
     - matrix endpoint
     - identity
     - Affine matrix to invert.

Parameters
----------

No additional fields.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - outputMatrix[i]
     - number; i=0..15
     - computed
     - Row-major matrix element; a whole outputMatrix endpoint is accepted by matrix consumers.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/inverseMatrix.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/inverseMatrix.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/inverseMatrix.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **1**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

This is an affine transform operation; validate degenerate and non-affine matrices against the intended contract.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

# docs/source/nodes/meshSurfaceFrames.rst

.. _node-meshSurfaceFrames:

meshSurfaceFrames
=================

Evaluate multiple surface attachment matrices from a declared mesh topology and UV layout.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Scoped batched surface attachment.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use for batched attachment evaluation when many outputs share a mesh input and topology.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - positionNX/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - static positionN vectors
     - Live positions indexed by mesh vertex.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - faces
     - integer[][]
     - required
     - Faces have at least three nonnegative vertex indices.
   * - uvs
     - number[2][]
     - required
     - UV coordinate table.
   * - faceVertexUvIndices; optional positionFaceVertexUvIndices
     - integer[]
     - required / same topology
     - Flattened per-face-vertex UV indices.
   * - attachments
     - attachment-record[]
     - required, nonempty
     - Each record declares faceIndex and coordinate; optional interpolation and frame policies are documented in surface contracts.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - outputMatrixN[i]
     - number; i=0..15
     - computed
     - Matrix element for attachment N.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/meshSurfaceFrames.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/meshSurfaceFrames.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/meshSurfaceFrames.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **0**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Preserve the declared input/output types, source units, and domain. Semantic validation is performed by the runtime compiler, not only the structural JSON schema.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

Related: :ref:`surfaceFrame <node-surfaceFrame>`.

See :doc:`surface record contracts <surface_contracts>`.


# docs/source/nodes/ModelNode.rst

.. _node-ModelNode:

ModelNode
=========

Evaluate a deterministic sparse-linear output model.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Validated model contract.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use for a compact affine response only after separate verification over the declared input domain.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - declared input names
     - number endpoints
     - required by terms
     - Named model features.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - backend
     - string
     - sparse_linear
     - Only sparse_linear is supported.
   * - outputs
     - named output-record object
     - required
     - Each output contains bias and weights or terms; terms contain input/weight.
   * - provenance
     - object
     - exporter requirement
     - Record domain, fit/validation split, sample counts, and error metrics in private port artifacts.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - declared output names
     - number
     - computed
     - bias + sum(weight * input).

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/ModelNode.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/ModelNode.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/ModelNode.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **7**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

ApproxNode shares the sparse-linear compiler path. Neither name proves approximation quality; report residuals on held-out observations.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.


# docs/source/nodes/motionPath.rst

.. _node-motionPath:

motionPath
==========

Evaluate position and scoped orientation along an open NURBS curve.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Scoped curve motion path.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use for captured path-follow behavior; distinguish raw parameter from fraction-mode arc-length traversal.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - parameter (aliases u/uValue)
     - number endpoint
     - 0
     - Parameter or normalized coordinate, depending on mode.
   * - controlPoints[i].x/y/z
     - number endpoints
     - static controlPoints
     - Live control-point components.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - degree
     - integer
     - node-specific
     - Open curve degree; require at least degree+1 CVs.
   * - controlPoints
     - number[3][]
     - required
     - Ordered CVs in one declared space.
   * - minValue / maxValue
     - numbers
     - 0 / 1
     - Parameter domain.
   * - fractionMode
     - boolean
     - false
     - Resolve traversal fraction to a curve parameter.
   * - worldUpVector
     - number[3]
     - [0,1,0]
     - Up-vector basis.
   * - rotateOrder
     - integer enum
     - 0
     - Maya rotate-order code 0..5.
   * - anglesInDegrees
     - boolean
     - true
     - Rotation output units.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - allCoordinatesX/Y/Z; rotateX/Y/Z
     - number
     - computed
     - Path position and Euler rotation.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/motionPath.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/motionPath.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/motionPath.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **1**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Preserve the declared input/output types, source units, and domain. Semantic validation is performed by the runtime compiler, not only the structural JSON schema.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

multiplyDivide
==============

Component-wise pass-through, multiply, divide, or power.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Exact numeric primitive.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use for independent XYZ arithmetic; this is not a vector dot or cross product.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - input1X/Y/Z; input2X/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - input1: 0; input2: 1
     - Component operands.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - operation
     - integer enum
     - 1
     - 0 pass input1; 1 multiply; 2 divide; 3 power.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - outputX / outputY / outputZ
     - number
     - computed
     - Independent component results.

Limits and porting notes

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

     - Default

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - matrices
     - array of number[16]
     - required unless indexed matrices are connected
     - Static matrices used when an input is not connected.

     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning

# docs/source/nodes/orientConstraint.rst

.. _node-orientConstraint:

orientConstraint
================

Compute a scoped weighted target orientation with captured basis and offsets.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Scoped constraint.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use when the source constraint's targets, spaces, weights, offset, and interpolation mode are all known.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - target[i].targetTranslateX/Y/Z; target[i].targetRotateX/Y/Z; target[i].targetScaleX/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - 0 / 0 / 1
     - Ordered target channels.
   * - target[i].targetWeight
     - number endpoint
     - target record weight, else 1
     - Dynamic target weight.
   * - constraintParentInverseMatrix; target[i].targetParentMatrix
     - matrix endpoints
     - identity
     - Source-space conversion for matrix-aware paths.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - targets
     - nonempty target-record[]
     - required
     - Records preserve translate, rotate, scale, weight, targetParentMatrix, and captured input offsets.
   * - normalize
     - boolean
     - true
     - Normalize scalar weighted paths by total weight.
   * - translateOffset / rotateOffset / scaleOffset
     - number[3]
     - 0 / 0 / 1
     - Captured maintain-offset behavior.
   * - matrixConstraint / matrixTranslateConstraint / matrixOrientConstraint
     - booleans
     - false
     - Select the scoped matrix-aware lowering path.
   * - interpType
     - static integer
     - captured source mode
     - Orientation interpolation support is path-specific; verify the exported mode.
   * - anglesInDegrees
     - boolean
     - true
     - Set false for radian-valued Euler/angle channels.
   * - rotateOrder
     - string
     - xyz
     - xyz, yzx, zxy, xzy, yxz, or zyx; check node-specific integer order fields.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - constraintRotateX/Y/Z
     - number
     - computed
     - Requested constraint channels; parentConstraint also exposes constraintRotateX/Y/Z.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/orientConstraint.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/orientConstraint.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/orientConstraint.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **0**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

The runtime does not discover a Maya DAG. Export all space/basis data. Multi-target rotation, zero total weights, nonpositive scales, and nondefault interpolation need explicit parity tests.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.


# docs/source/nodes/pairBlend.rst

.. _node-pairBlend:

pairBlend
=========

Blend translation and rotation channels, with scoped quaternion rotation interpolation.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Scoped transform blend.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use for captured two-source transform blending; use matrix constraints for target-space conversion.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - inTranslate1X/Y/Z; inTranslate2X/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - 0
     - Translation sources.
   * - inRotate1X/Y/Z; inRotate2X/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - 0
     - Euler rotation sources.
   * - weight
     - number endpoint
     - 0
     - Weight from source 1 toward source 2.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - translateXMode/YMode/ZMode; rotateMode
     - static integer enums
     - 0
     - 0 blend, 1 source 1, 2 source 2.
   * - rotInterpolation
     - static integer enum
     - 0
     - 0 Euler, 1 quaternion.
   * - roundWeight; exactSlerp
     - booleans
     - false
     - Optional rounding and exact spherical interpolation controls.
   * - anglesInDegrees
     - boolean
     - true
     - Set false for radian-valued Euler/angle channels.
   * - rotateOrder
     - string
     - xyz
     - xyz, yzx, zxy, xzy, yxz, or zyx; check node-specific integer order fields.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - outTranslateX/Y/Z; outRotateX/Y/Z
     - number
     - computed
     - Requested transform component.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/pairBlend.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/pairBlend.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/pairBlend.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **1**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Selection modes, interpolation mode, and rotate order must be static. Unsupported dynamic mode connections fail compilation.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

   * - rotateOrder
     - string
     - xyz
     - xyz, yzx, zxy, xzy, yxz, or zyx; check node-specific integer order fields.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - constraintTranslateX/Y/Z
     - number
     - computed
     - Requested constraint channels; parentConstraint also exposes constraintRotateX/Y/Z.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/pointConstraint.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/pointConstraint.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/pointConstraint.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **0**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

The runtime does not discover a Maya DAG. Export all space/basis data. Multi-target rotation, zero total weights, nonpositive scales, and nondefault interpolation need explicit parity tests.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

# docs/source/nodes/RbfNode.rst

.. _node-RbfNode:

RbfNode
=======

Evaluate explicit radial basis centers and output coefficient vectors.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Explicit RBF contract.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use for an RBF with a known kernel and coefficients, or a separately validated fitted response; do not equate training-center agreement with domain accuracy.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - names in input_order
     - named number endpoints
     - required
     - One input endpoint for every declared dimension.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - input_order
     - nonempty string[]
     - required
     - Ordered input dimensions.
   * - centers
     - number[][]
     - required, nonempty
     - Each center dimension matches input_order.
   * - kernel
     - string enum
     - required
     - gaussian, polyharmonic_1, cubic, thin_plate, multiquadric, inverse_quadratic, inverse_multiquadric.
   * - outputs
     - object of coefficient records
     - required
     - Each output has exactly one coefficients array with one value per center.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - declared output names
     - number
     - computed
     - Kernel-weighted response.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/RbfNode.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/RbfNode.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/RbfNode.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **1**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Coefficients are evaluation coefficients, not automatically solved from target samples. Input scaling and domain selection belong to the exporter.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

     - required

     - string
     - required

# docs/source/nodes/SampledNode.rst

.. _node-SampledNode:

SampledNode
===========

Represent behavior with explicit sampled tables and a declared interpolation policy.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Validated sampled contract.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use when the sample-domain contract is intentional and quantified; it is not equivalent to reconstructing an arbitrary solver.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - x / y; or names in input_order
     - number endpoints
     - 0 / declared endpoints
     - Table coordinates or nearest-center dimensions.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - interpolation
     - string enum
     - linear1d
     - linear1d (aliases linear/piecewise_linear), bilinear2d (alias bilinear), nearest (aliases nearestnd/nearest_nd/exact_centers).
   * - x / values
     - matching number[]
     - required for linear1d
     - Ordered input axis and scalar samples.
   * - x_axis / y_axis; grid (or flattened values)
     - number[]; number[][] or number[]
     - required for bilinear2d
     - Axes each contain at least 2 values; grid shape matches axis lengths.
   * - input_order / centers / outputs
     - string[] / number[][] / output records
     - required for nearest path
     - Nearest-center inputs and one output value per center.
   * - bias
     - number
     - 0
     - Optional output bias in the nearest-center path.
   * - provenance
     - object
     - exporter requirement
     - Sampling coverage, input domain, and independent verification evidence.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - output
     - number
     - computed
     - Scalar result.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/SampledNode.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/SampledNode.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/SampledNode.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **0.5**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Grid paths clamp at the sampled domain edge; nearest-center evaluation can be discontinuous. Test interiors, boundaries, and unseen combinations.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

# docs/source/nodes/ScalarMathNode.rst

.. _node-ScalarMathNode:

ScalarMathNode
==============

Apply a source-neutral scalar math operation.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Exact numeric primitive.

**Aliases:** ``MathNode``.

When to use
-----------

Use when a formula has a direct numeric expression rather than a Maya-specific node contract.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - input (aliases in/x/a/value)
     - number endpoint or parameter
     - 0
     - Unary operand.
   * - a / b
     - number endpoints or parameters
     - 0; b=1 for multiply/divide/power
     - Binary operands; input1/input2 and indexed aliases are supported.
   * - min / max; t
     - number endpoints or parameters
     - 0 / 1; 0
     - Clamp bounds or lerp weight, as required by op.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - op (alias operation)
     - string enum
     - identity
     - identity, negate, abs, add, subtract, multiply, divide, min, max, power, clamp, saturate, lerp, one_minus, sqrt, tan, acos, atan2.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - output
     - number
     - computed
     - Scalar result.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/ScalarMathNode.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/ScalarMathNode.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/ScalarMathNode.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **5**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

Trigonometric operations use radians. Guard invalid numeric domains in the source graph; validate divide-by-zero and power edge cases explicitly.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.


# docs/source/nodes/scaleConstraint.rst

.. _node-scaleConstraint:

scaleConstraint
===============

Compute a weighted geometric scale, rather than an arithmetic mean.

**Layer:** portable graph node. **Contract:** Scoped constraint.

**Aliases:** none.

When to use
-----------

Use when the source constraint's targets, spaces, weights, offset, and interpolation mode are all known.

Inputs
------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - target[i].targetTranslateX/Y/Z; target[i].targetRotateX/Y/Z; target[i].targetScaleX/Y/Z
     - number endpoints
     - 0 / 0 / 1
     - Ordered target channels.
   * - target[i].targetWeight
     - number endpoint
     - target record weight, else 1
     - Dynamic target weight.
   * - constraintParentInverseMatrix; target[i].targetParentMatrix
     - matrix endpoints
     - identity
     - Source-space conversion for matrix-aware paths.

Parameters
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - targets
     - nonempty target-record[]
     - required
     - Records preserve translate, rotate, scale, weight, targetParentMatrix, and captured input offsets.
   * - normalize
     - boolean
     - true
     - Normalize scalar weighted paths by total weight.
   * - translateOffset / rotateOffset / scaleOffset
     - number[3]
     - 0 / 0 / 1
     - Captured maintain-offset behavior.
   * - matrixConstraint / matrixTranslateConstraint / matrixOrientConstraint
     - booleans
     - false
     - Select the scoped matrix-aware lowering path.
   * - interpType
     - static integer
     - captured source mode
     - Orientation interpolation support is path-specific; verify the exported mode.
   * - anglesInDegrees
     - boolean
     - true
     - Set false for radian-valued Euler/angle channels.
   * - rotateOrder
     - string
     - xyz
     - xyz, yzx, zxy, xzy, yxz, or zyx; check node-specific integer order fields.

Outputs
-------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 20 15 40

   * - Name
     - Type
     - Default
     - Meaning
   * - constraintScaleX/Y/Z
     - number
     - computed
     - Requested constraint channels; parentConstraint also exposes constraintRotateX/Y/Z.

Usage and verification
----------------------

Download :download:`the complete synthetic graph <../../../examples/graph/scaleConstraint.json>`.

.. literalinclude:: ../../../examples/graph/scaleConstraint.json
   :language: json

.. code-block:: console

   orgctl eval examples/graph/scaleConstraint.json --output json

Expected ``result``: **1**, absolute tolerance ``1e-05``.

Limits and porting notes
------------------------

The runtime does not discover a Maya DAG. Export all space/basis data. Multi-target rotation, zero total weights, nonpositive scales, and nondefault interpolation need explicit parity tests.

See :doc:`common contracts <contracts>` for endpoint syntax, numeric domains, units, and error handling.

# docs/source/nodes/surface_contracts.rst

Surface attachment and cage records
===================================

meshSurfaceFrames attachments
-----------------------------

Every attachment declares faceIndex and coordinate=[u,v]. Preserve vertex,
face-vertex UV, and attachment ordering. Optional capture records select an
explicit policy; they do not discover source semantics at runtime.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1

   * - Fields
     - Type / constraint
     - Meaning
   * - normalAxis / tangentAxis
     - integer; defaults 0 / 2
     - Frame axis assignment.
   * - positionVertexIndices / positionWeights
     - integer[] / matching number[]
     - Explicit position support.
   * - triangleVertexIndices / barycentricWeights
     - integer[3] / number[3]
     - Triangle interpolation.
   * - frameVertexIndices / normalWeights
     - integer[] / matching number[]
     - Normal interpolation support.
   * - tangentWeights / tangentPositionWeights
     - number[] matching support
     - Tangent interpolation; position weights select the position-based path.
   * - normalVertexIndices / normalMatrixWeights
     - 1..32 integer indices / 9 numbers per vertex
     - Explicit affine normal support.
   * - tangentVertexIndices / tangentMatrixWeights / tangentAnchorVertex
     - 1..32 indices / 9 numbers per vertex / integer
     - Explicit affine tangent support and anchor.
   * - tangentMode
     - string
     - Empty default, firstTriangle, firstTriangleFixed13, firstTriangleFixed02,
       firstTriangleFixed023, or firstTriangleFixed123.
   * - vertexNormalMode
     - string
     - Empty default, simple, or simpleLocal.
   * - tangentSign / positionFloat32
     - number / boolean; defaults 1 / false
     - Orientation sign and reduced-precision position policy.

Verify nondefault frame policies independently. Do not adjust them solely to
reduce final error without proving the upstream intended contract.

weightedVertexCage centers
--------------------------

Each record has centerFaceVertex (integer), normalOppositePairs (two integer
vertex pairs), tangentEdgeNeighbor (integer), weightsByCageVertex (one finite
nonnegative weight per cage output), and restLocalCageOffsets (one finite XYZ
offset per output). References belong to faceVertexIndices. Weights across
centers sum to one for each output point. Verify frame orientation and geometry
on independent synthetic input; rest offsets cannot hide missing dependencies.
